sentences: I turn the coarse focus knob to lower the stage until the slide is close to the objective lens.
I place a drop of immersion oil on the slide before switching to the 100x objective.
I clean the eyepiece lens with lens paper after every session to remove dust.
I adjust the condenser to match the numerical aperture of the objective in use.
I check the light bulb and replace it if the illumination is uneven or dim.
I rotate the nosepiece to select the 10x objective and click it into place.
I prepare a wet mount by placing a drop of pond water on a clean glass slide.
I lower the cover slip slowly at an angle to avoid trapping air bubbles.
I measure the diameter of the field of view at each magnification using a stage micrometer.
I wipe the stage with 70 percent ethanol to remove any residue from previous samples.
I store the microscope with the dust cover on and the lowest objective in position.
I record the magnification of the eyepiece and objective to calculate total magnification.
I center the specimen in the field of view before I increase the magnification.
I use a mechanical stage to move the slide smoothly along the x and y axes.
I check the diaphragm setting to control the amount of light passing through the specimen.
I apply a drop of methylene blue to the specimen and wait one minute before rinsing.
I align the binocular eyepieces by adjusting the interpupillary distance to match my eyes.
I focus the condenser by moving it up or down until the light is sharp on the slide.
I clean the objective lenses with a cotton swab and a small amount of alcohol.
I calibrate the ocular micrometer with a stage micrometer to measure cell dimensions.
